### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s).

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via sys_metadata_activation (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/actions/_activation (route, a path literal in WHERE_PLATFORM_ACTION))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via sys_metadata_activation (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via sys_metadata_activation (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 81 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `44a36dce396a8b7fab80fa61c2456a53855c1bdb` — the merge of head `5122812f3e18e2e5529223e1433db5d733649297` into base `e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 44a36dce396a8b7fab80fa61c2456a53855c1bdb && git checkout 44a36dce396a8b7fab80fa61c2456a53855c1bdb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7 5122812f3e18e2e5529223e1433db5d733649297 && git checkout -B drift-repro e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7 && git merge --no-ff 5122812f3e18e2e5529223e1433db5d733649297

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e05445e4f5c5ca2dad6aabbb9226a3dc564e55d7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Read three things: the switch is drawn disabled with the reason, a click sends no `POST`, and the operator under the same posture gets a live switch.

**M2. Four changed files are outside the claim surface.** That surface is claim 6943333260 plus amendment 6943362097.
- `packages/objectql/src/action-activation.ts` and `packages/objectql/src/engine-actions.ts`. These are published source. The claim names only `action-activation.test.ts`. Ruling 6944409840 brings into scope the sentence in `packages/types/**`, not objectql source.

**M3. The Clause-② line does not name two published widenings.** The claim, the body and the changeset all say `yes (narrowing: … ; widening: new studio-namespace locale keys)`. The diff also widens two published APIs:
- **`@objectstack/types`.** `describeTurnedOffPackagedItem(kind, options?)` gains an optional argument and a new exported `TurnedOffPackagedItemOptions` (re-exported from the package index).
- **`@objectstack/objectql`.** The exported `ActionActivationProjection` gains `disabledPackageOf(name)`, and `describeDisabled(name, platform?)` gains an optional argument.

Both are additive, and their only callers are in this diff. Please restate the line in the claim amendment, the PR body and the changeset, so the seat's L2 at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER reads the whole face.

  - or rule item 5 out of this PR, put it on the deviation list, and leave a follow-up card.

- **Wording.** The Clause-② text says "the public `PackagedActionsPage` export of `@object-ui/app-shell`", while the ADR-0087 note in the same changeset rightly calls the package private. ### ① Derived judgments

What ships to a deployment is the console built from it: the `automation:packaged-actions` component ref is no longer registered, and the route `component/automation/packaged-actions` redirects ahead of `component/:ns/:name/*`, so a nav entry or bookmark naming the ref lands in Studio instead of on an unresolved component. ### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the spec and the rulings. What leaves is a console surface, by the maintainer's word on the card (「打包动作不是应该在 studio 对应的软件包中自定义吗」). For an app's action the capability is re-homed in the same change (object Actions view, standalone item page), over the unchanged doors. For a platform action the console switch goes for good, by 「同意，立卡」, and ruling 6944409840 (A, 「保持原状并写明恢复方法」) keeps existing rows in force with the door as the recovery. No spec-declared capability is taken from a consumer: `disabledActions`, the ledger read, the write door and its two authority gates (`refuseUngrantedActivationAuthoring`, `refuseUngrantedActivationWrite`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts:188–191`) are byte-unchanged. The narrowing holds.

`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`. The sentence had to change (it named a page that no longer exists) and its first consumer, the metadata read that serves `disabledActions`, is untouched. Holds, with N1.

`docs/adr/0146-…md`, D4 amendment. Add-only (+21 −0). Checked sentence by sentence against the tree:
- "on a read-only app package, each vendor action carries the switch, on the object's Actions view … on the item's page" — `ObjectActionsPanel.tsx` (`disabled` and a non-org route package), `ResourceEditPage.tsx` (`hostReadOnly`, `type === 'action'`). Holds.
- "the flow switch's control, words, pre-judged gate and verbatim refusals" — `FlowLedgerSwitch` reused, `useFlowLedgerWalledReadOnly`, `actionErrorDetail` verbatim. Holds.
- "the read is the `sys_metadata_activation` list … the write `POST /api/v1/actions/_activation/:object/:action` … its gate the same `refuseUngrantedActivationWrite`" — `packagedActionLedger.ts`; `actions.ts:190`. Holds.
- "The platform's own actions carry no switch anywhere in the console" — `isAppPackageListed` offers a switch only for a listed package without the `kernel` flag; `parsePackages` leaves a manifest-scoped `system`/`cloud` package out of the list and flags a flat-scoped one, and an unreadable list answers no switch. Pinned by three cases in `ObjectActionsPanel.ledgerSwitch-34724.test.tsx` and one in the item-page test. Holds on the object view; see N2 for the item page.
- Ruling 6944409840: "A row that already switches a platform action off stays in force: no boot or upgrade step re-enables it … the server door is not changed … Turning one on again is the activation door's `{ enabled: true }`, and the `ACTION_DISABLED` sentence for a platform action names that door rather than Studio." Each clause matches the ruling comment, and the tree: no boot or upgrade step is added, `actions.ts` is not in the diff, and `engine-actions.ts` judges the row's package against the registry manifest (`scope` `system` or `cloud`), pinned in `action-activation.test.ts` and live on `sys_user` `ban_user` in `api-action-door-forward.dogfood.test.ts`.
